translations.text: James, servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes: greetings!
Count it all joy, my brothers, when you fall into various kinds of trials,
knowing that the testing of your faith produces patience.
And let patience have its perfect work, so that you may be perfect and wholly sound, lacking in nothing.
But if any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask of God, who gives to all generously and reproaches no one, and he will give it to him.
But let him ask in faith and without doubting, for whoever doubts is like a wave of the sea, stirred up and tossed about by the wind.
Let that man not suppose that he will receive anything from God.
A double-minded man is unstable in all his ways.
Let the lowly brother boast in his exaltation,
and the rich man in his humiliation, for like the flower of the grass, so he will pass away.
For the sun rose with its heat and withered the grass, and its flower fell, and the beauty of its appearance passed away. So too the rich man will wither away in his going.
Blessed is the man who endures trial, for he will be proven and will receive the crown of life, which God promised to those who love him.
Let no one who is tempted say, "I am being tempted by God," for God cannot be tempted by evil, and he tempts no one.
Rather, each person is tempted by his own desire; he is drawn away and deceived.
Then desire conceives and gives birth to sin, and sin, when it is complete, gives birth to death.
Do not be deceived, my beloved brothers!
Every good thing given and every perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of light, with whom there is no change or shadow of turning.
He willed it and gave birth to us by the word of truth, so that we might be a kind of beginning of his creatures.
Now therefore, my beloved brothers, let every person be quick to hear, slow to speak, slow to anger.
For a man's anger does not produce the righteousness of God.
Therefore put away from yourselves all filthiness and the excess of wickedness, and with meekness receive the implanted word, which is able to save your souls.
And be doers of the word, and not only hearers who hold yourselves in contempt.
If anyone is only a hearer of the word and not a doer, such a person is like a man who looks at the face of his form in a mirror.
For he looked at himself and went away, and at once forgot what he was like.
But whoever has looked into the perfect law of freedom and remained in it has become not a hearer who forgets but a doer of the work; this person will be blessed in his doing.
If anyone among you thinks that he is a servant of God, and does not bridle his tongue but deceives his heart, this man's service is vain.
Service that is pure and undefiled before God and the Father is this: to look after orphans and widows in their affliction, and to keep oneself undefiled by this world.
My brothers, do not hold the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory, with partiality.
For if a man with a gold ring and splendid clothing comes into your assembly, and a poor man in shabby clothing also comes in,
and you look to the one who is wearing the splendid clothing and say to him, "You sit here in a good place," and to the poor man you say, "You stand over there," or, "Sit here below our feet,"
have you not made distinctions among yourselves and become judges with evil thoughts of the heart?
Listen, my beloved brothers: has God not chosen the poor of the world to be rich in faith and heirs of the kingdom, which he promised to those who love him?
But you have dishonored the poor man. Is it not the rich who oppress you, and is it not they who drag you into court?
Is it not they who blaspheme the good name that is called upon you?
If you fulfill the royal law according to the Scripture, "You shall love your neighbor as yourself," you do well.
But if you show partiality, you commit sin and are convicted by the law as transgressors of the law.
For whoever keeps the whole law but stumbles in one point has become guilty of all of it.
For he who said, "Do not commit adultery," also said, "Do not murder." If you do not commit adultery but you murder, you have become a transgressor of the law.
So speak and so act as those who are to be judged by the law of freedom.
For judgment is without mercy to those who have not shown mercy. Boast in the mercy of judgment.
What profit is it, my brothers, if someone says, "I have faith," but does not have works? Can faith alone save him?
For if a brother or sister is naked and lacking daily food,
and one of you says to them, "Go in peace, be filled and be warmed," and you do not give them what the body needs, what profit is it?
So also faith: if it does not have works, it is simply dead.
But someone may say, "You have faith and I have works." Show me your faith from your works, and I will show you my faith from my works.
You believe that God is one; you do well. The demons also believe, and they tremble before him.
Do you want to know, O vain man, that faith without works is dead?
Was not Abraham our father justified by works, when he offered Isaac his son upon the altar?
Do you see that faith helped his works, and by works that faith was made complete?
And the Scripture was fulfilled that says, "Abraham believed God, and it was reckoned to him as righteousness," and he was called the friend of God.
Do you see that a person is justified by works, and not by faith alone?
In the same way, was not Rahab the harlot also justified by works, when she received the messengers and sent them out by another way?
For as the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without works is dead.
Do not many of you become teachers, my brothers! Know that we will receive a greater judgment.
For we all stumble greatly. Whoever does not stumble in speech is a perfect man; he is able to bridle the whole body as well.
If we put bridles on a horse to make it obey us, we turn it and its whole body.
Look at ships too: though they are very large and driven about by fierce winds, they are turned by a small rudder wherever their pilot wants to go.
So also the tongue is a small member, yet it boasts greatly. See how much material a small fire sets ablaze!

And the tongue is likewise a fire, an ornament of falsehood. The tongue is set among our members; it defiles the whole body and sets on fire the wheel of creation, and it is itself set on fire by Gehenna.
For every kind of beast and bird, of creeping thing and swimming creature, is tamed and has been tamed by humankind.
But no one is able to tame the human tongue: an unrestrainable evil, full of deadly poison.
For with it we bless God and the Father, and with it we curse people, who are made in the likeness of God.
Blessing and cursing come out of the same mouth. My beloved brothers, it is not right for this to be so.
Does sweet and bitter water flow from the same opening of a spring?
Can a fig tree, my brothers, bear olives, or a vine figs? In the same way, no single spring can bring forth both salty and sweet water.
Who among you is wise and understanding? Let him show his works by his good conduct, in the meekness of wisdom.
But if you have bitter envy and rivalry in your hearts, do not boast and lie against the truth.
This is not the wisdom that comes down from above, but is earthly, unspiritual, and devilish.
For where there is envy and rivalry, there is disorder and every evil deed.
But the wisdom from above is first of all purity, and then peace, kindness, and obedience; it is full of mercy and the fruit of good works, impartial and without hypocrisy.
For the fruit of righteousness is sown in peace by those who make peace.
Where do the wars and quarrels among you come from? Do they not come from your own desires, which are at war in your members?
You desire and do not have; you kill and are envious, and cannot obtain; you quarrel and fight, and do not have, because you do not ask.
You ask and do not receive, because you ask wrongly, so that you may spend it on your desires.
Fornicators and adulterers! Do you not know that love of this world is enmity with God? So whoever wants to be a friend of this world sets himself up as an enemy of God.
Or do you think that the Scripture speaks in vain: "The spirit that dwells in us longs even to the point of jealousy"?
But he gives greater grace. That is why it says: "God crushes the proud, but gives grace to the humble."
Submit yourselves to God and resist the devil, and he will flee from you.
Draw near to God, and he will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, you sinners, and make your hearts pure, you double-minded.
Be humbled, and weep and mourn. Let your laughter be turned into mourning and your joy into sorrow.
Humble yourselves before the Lord, and he will exalt you.

Do not speak evil of one another, my brothers. Whoever speaks evil about a brother and judges his brother judges the law and condemns the law. If you condemn the law, you are not a doer of the law but a judge.
There is one lawgiver and judge, who is able to save and to destroy. Who are you to judge your neighbour?
Now you too, who say: "Today or tomorrow let us go to such-and-such a city, and spend a year there, and trade, and make a profit":
you do not know what tomorrow will bring. For what is your life? You are like smoke, which appears for a little while and then vanishes.
Instead, you ought to say: "If the Lord wills, we shall live and do this or that."
But now you boast in your arrogance. All such boasting is evil.
Whoever knows the good thing to do and does not do it, for him it is sin.
Now then, you rich, weep and wail over the miseries that are coming upon you.
Your riches have rotted, and moths have eaten your clothing.
Your gold and your silver have rusted, and their rust will be a witness against you and will eat your flesh like fire. You have stored up treasure in the last days.
Behold, the wages of the labourers who mowed your fields, which you held back, cry out, and the cries of the reapers have reached the ears of the Lord of Sabaoth.
You have lived in luxury on the earth and indulged yourselves. You have fattened your bodies as for a day of slaughter.
You have condemned and killed the righteous one, and he does not resist you.
So be patient, brothers, until the coming of the Lord. Behold, the farmer waits for the precious fruit of the earth and is patient over it until it receives the early and the late rain.
You too be patient. Strengthen your hearts, for the coming of the Lord is near.
Do not grumble against one another, brothers, so that you may not be judged. Behold, the judge is standing at the doors.
My brothers, take as your example of suffering hardship and of patience the prophets who spoke in the name of the Lord.
Behold, we call those who endured blessed. You have heard of the endurance of Job, and you have seen the outcome the Lord gave, for he is full of mercy and compassion.
Above all, my brothers, do not swear, either by heaven or by earth or by any other oath. Let your yes be yes and your no be no, so that you do not fall into duplicity.
If any of you is in distress, let him pray; if anyone is cheerful, let him sing praise.
If anyone among you is sick, let him call the elders of the church, and let them pray over him and anoint him with oil in the name of the Lord.
And the prayer of faith will save the sick one, and the Lord will raise him up. And if he has committed any sin, it will be forgiven him.
Confess your sins to one another and pray for one another, so that you may be healed, for the prayer of a righteous person is very powerful in helping.
Elijah was a man just like us, and he prayed that it would not rain, and it did not rain on the earth for three years and six months.
And he prayed again, and the sky gave rain, and the earth brought forth its fruit.
Brothers, if anyone among you strays from the truth and someone turns him back,
let them know that whoever turns a sinner back from the way of his error will save his own soul from death and will cover a multitude of sins.
